title: Candidate feedback draft: Samuel Hill — Senior Backend Engineer
interview_rounds: phone-screen (30m), take-home (48h), onsite loop: coding + system design + behavioural
overall_recommendation: consider-with-reservations — follow up on systems design and operational experience
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad (Priya)

Context: Candidate applied for Senior Backend Engineer focused on serving runtime optimizations. Refs: internal posting, take-home prompt (KV cache + batching microservice).

Phone screen (30m) — 2026-03-10, Alex Kim
- High-level background: 8+ years infra/backend, previous at cloud infra startup, strong C++ + Go experience.
- Quick convo about latency-first systems, story about reducing p95 by 2x at prior role (kept it high level).
- Phone screen pass; invited to take-home.

Take-home (submitted 2026-03-18) — 48h window
- What I saw:
- Implemented prototype in Go, clean code, good tests.
- Approach: simple single-process service with in-memory prefix cache and batching.
- Strengths: clear code structure, unit tests, thoughtful benchmarking script.
- Weaknesses: missed async worker model for batching under high concurrency; no discussion of KV cache eviction policy at scale.
- Score: 4/5 for coding quality; incomplete operational considerations.

Onsite loop (2026-03-26) — my notes from system design + coding + behavioural:
- Coding (pairing): solved algorithmic portion; used appropriate data structures. Slightly slower to implement edge-case handling but final solution acceptable.
- System design (45m): asked to design a serving component for prefix-caching and batching across models. Candidate proposed sharded workers, local LRU caches, TTL per model.
  - Positives: Reasonable partitioning and awareness of cross-tenant isolation. Brought up metrics and basic SLOs.
  - Concerns: missed discussion of KV cache consistency across replicas (staleness), incremental rollout strategies, and fallback paths if worker queue saturates. Limited depth on quantization/latency tradeoffs.
- Behavioural: good collaboration examples, ownership stories, handled conflict well. Clear expectations on code reviews and on-call.

Strengths:
- Strong coding hygiene, tests, pragmatic engineering tradeoffs for short deadlines.
- Good backend language experience (Go/C++), comfortable with low-level perf debugging.
- Good culture fit with eng-serving-runtime team values (ship fast, measure).

Concerns / Risks:
- Systems design depth for highly distributed serving at multi-tenant scale could be shallow; needs follow-up on cache coordination and graceful degradation strategies.
- Communication in whiteboard/design felt somewhat high-level; would like evidence of designing for failure modes (backpressure, circuit breakers, prioritization).
- Not much public experience with model-serving specifics like KV cache offload to remote store or batching across GPU devices. Could learn, but ramp risk.

Suggested next steps:
- Do a focused technical follow-up: 60m deep-dive on cache coordination and backpressure handling (invite 1 backend lead + 1 infra SRE).
- If deep-dive satisfactory, consider hire at L4 with mentorship ramp plan (pair on first release, shadow on incident handling).
- Ask candidate for a short writeup (1-2 pages) on how they would evolve their take-home to support multi-region, multi-tenant production (pay attention to consistency, cost, and rollout).

Hiring rec (draft):
- "Proceed to technical deep-dive" — not an immediate hire; leaning toward hire if candidate demonstrates deeper operational design.

Open questions / TODO (for debrief):
- Confirm availability for follow-up interview next week.
- Check references for specific infra projects (cache sharding, eviction) — add question about scaling KV caches across replicas.
- Compensation banding: likely L4. Need to validate with recruiting.

Quotes from interviewers:
- Alex K: "Solid engineer, great code, would be a reliable IC. Needs systems depth for edge cases."
- Maya T: "Good communicator in 1:1s, but design discussion didn't dig into failure cases."

Notes to self: keep feedback factual and actionable. Emphasize specific examples where candidate did/didn't address production edge cases.
